coverage: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-23 (Asia/Bangkok, UTC+7). First issue, so it looks back one week, with a short catch-up of LINE Developers notices from Nov 9 to 13 and the LINE Taiwan CONVERGE report.
summary: A breach at COMSBI, a third-party LINE integration tool, exposed LINE OA friend data at 16 Japanese companies, including 1.37 million Nissin friends. The Messaging API now rejects Flex Messages nested deeper than 20 boxes. LINE and Thailand's Finance Ministry launch a one-year SME AI and LINE OA program, and Fukuoka ships a Gemini-powered LINE MINI App.

items.topic: Top story: LINE OA friend data leaked through a third-party SaaS (Japan)
items.title: COMSBI breach: one support account exposed LINE OA friend data of 16 companies
items.summary: Sonicmoov said an attacker used stolen credentials for its own internal support accounts to log in to COMSBI (SaaS edition), a cloud LINE integration tool, from 23:04 on Nov 9 to the morning of Nov 10 JST, and pulled data for multiple client companies plus cloud config and credentials. Leaked fields include LINE user IDs, display names, profile images and status messages of OA friends, and for some clients names, phone numbers, emails and addresses. Fixes promised: mandatory 2FA on the admin console, IP restrictions, rate limits on bulk reads, and rotation of the LINE OA integration credentials.

items.topic: Top story: LINE OA friend data leaked through a third-party SaaS (Japan)
items.title: Nissin Foods: 1,374,157 LINE OA friends affected, including people who never entered the campaign
items.summary: Nissin's agency TOPPAN ran a LINE campaign on COMSBI. The tool required importing the whole OA friend list before the draw, so friends who never entered (and some who had blocked the account) were exposed; 543 winners also lost name, address and phone. Nissin says its own OA channel credentials were not taken. The design lesson: do not sync the full follower list into a campaign tool you do not control.

items.title: Heiwado: up to 328,976 friends of its shop OAs affected
items.summary: Retailer Heiwado used COMSBI directly for the CoCoRo Plus, kids fest and GOODS DEPO accounts. Leaked: LINE display name, profile image, LINE user ID, gender, birth year and month, and postcode to city level. By Nov 20, CyberWatch.jp counted 16 affected organizations, 761,511 people and 1,458,608 records in their public notices.

items.topic: LINE Platform and API changes
items.title: Messaging API: Flex Message box nesting is now capped at 20 levels
items.summary: Since Nov 19, a Flex Message whose boxes nest deeper than 20 levels (the outermost box is level 1) gets 400 Bad Request. Before this there was no limit. Bots that generate Flex layouts recursively, for example from LLM output or templates, should check their depth.

items.topic: LINE Platform and API changes
items.title: LY Corporation ends official support for LINE Developer Community in Japan
items.summary: Official support ends at the end of 2026. The community, started in February 2019, continues from 2027 as the volunteer-run L-Developer Community on connpass and Discord. Its founder Kazumasa Yamamoto said that official docs and AI now make the APIs easier to use, so what to build matters more.

items.topic: Thailand
items.title: LINE and Thailand's Finance Ministry announce SME AI training, anti-fraud and disaster alert plans
items.summary: Deputy PM and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas visited LY Corporation in Tokyo on Nov 19. Plan one is a one-year SME program with at least 10 practical courses taught by LINE Certified Coaches (LINE OA, content, CRM, targeted ads, AI for planning, campaign analysis and customer replies), aiming for 5,000 on-site trainees a year and about 300,000 online views. LINE adds 22,000 benefits worth about 10.5 million baht (LINE POINTS, LINE OA chat package discounts, LINE Ads credits). The other two plans cover scam prevention and disaster alerts. PRD adds that BOI will look at task-specific AI agent tools for SMEs.

items.topic: Thailand
items.title: FLAIR BKK'26: 45% of Thai luxury buyers buy through LINE chat; LINE previews OA Team Management
items.summary: LINE Thailand survey figures: 45% buy luxury goods through LINE chat, over 94% of luxury-brand OA followers say OA messages raise purchase intent, and average friend counts of luxury OAs grew 19%. Shoppers accept AI chatbots for routine questions but want human staff for advice. LINE plans an OA Team Management feature where sales staff chat with customers from the brand OA, with assignment, saved chat history and a dashboard, so the relationship stays with the brand when staff change.

items.topic: Thailand
items.title: Khon Kaen University blood bank reaches 96.4% of donors with LINE OA plus telemedicine
items.summary: KKU's blood center used LINE OA messages and appointments, then video or voice consults with two-step identity checks, and fell back to phone and letters. It confirmed contact with 162 of 168 donors who needed follow-up. A small but concrete Thai healthcare case for LINE OA workflows.

items.topic: Japan
items.title: Fukuoka City launches an AI waste-sorting LINE MINI App on Nov 24
items.summary: LY Communications and Fukuoka City launch Gomi Shirube: take a photo or type an item name, and generative AI (Gemini API) gives the city's sorting category and disposal tips, in 11 languages, with no install or signup. It replaces the city OA's keyword search, which got over 30,000 lookups a month in 2024. It will also be reachable from the @fukuokacity OA from about Jan 15, 2027. In an Oct 2026 survey of 78 users, 98.7% said they would keep using it.

items.title: LY Corporation's Agent i comes to LINE MUSIC as AI PlayList
items.summary: Agent i, LY's merged AI agent brand (formerly Yahoo! JAPAN AI Assistant and LINE AI), now builds and suggests playlists inside LINE MUSIC 6.39.0+, with LINE Login required. LY says the feature uses Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform or the OpenAI API, and will reach Agent i in the LINE app and Yahoo! JAPAN app later.

items.topic: Japan
items.title: LINE client team runs coding agents in the cloud: 375 to about 12,000 tasks a month in four months
items.summary: LY engineer onevcat describes Agent Cluster, an in-house platform that runs coding agents in the cloud under LY's security rules, with no tokens handed to agents and CI reworked for agent-paced verification. Monthly tasks grew from 375 to nearly 12,000 while total cost grew 7.5 times.

items.topic: AI chatbot builders and developer community
items.title: Dify 1.20.0: new human-in-the-loop approvals over IM, but LINE is not one of the channels
items.summary: Dify 1.20.0 adds New HITL: approval requests can go out by email and through Slack, Feishu/Lark, Microsoft Teams, DingTalk or WeCom. LINE is not in the list, so LINE-based Dify bots still need a plugin (for example the community LINE Connect plugin) or a custom webhook. The release also adds OpenTelemetry trace export, Langfuse v4 support and malware scanning of knowledge uploads.

items.title: LINE Taiwan targets Q1 2027 for an AI Agent Platform inside LINE Official Accounts
items.summary: LY's report on LINE CONVERGE 2026 says Taiwan has over 3.6 million LINE Official Accounts (as of Aug 2026) and 22 million monthly users. LINE Taiwan plans an AI Agent Platform that lets businesses build their own agents inside their OA, starting in Q1 2027. iThome reported on Oct 13 that the platform is no-code, starts with booking, sales and customer service agents, and will support MCP.
